clue.text: Absurdly complex to find birds on barren land to west

indicators.note: in an across entry the west side is the left, so the heath comes first

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
robins are birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's instructions for spotting birds on moorland to the west, oddly called absurdly complex.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist who drew absurdly elaborate contraptions; his name became an adjective for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist's name is used as an adjective for ludicrously elaborate makeshift machinery.

clue.text: Condiment Arab possibly put on most of raw food

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on top of the next comes before it

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, hence 'possibly'

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a dish is an item of food

explanation.surface: A recipe in which an Arab adds a condiment to raw food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person, but it is the horse breed; 'most of' trims the final W from 'raw'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot pungent root sauce is a classic condiment for roast beef.

clue.text: A European said to be so bitter?

indicators.note: said signals that the sound of the phrase gives the answer

parts.note: a Serb is a European, from Serbia

explanation.surface: A question asking whether some European is said to be bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a literary adjective meaning sour or harsh in taste or temper.

clue.text: Fervently believed explosive material about creative works

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces go around the next one

parts.note: HE is short for high explosive
felt is a fabric
art is the product of creative work

explanation.surface: Someone describes explosives packed around works of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive material' reads as one phrase, but the two words split, and 'about' sends them round the creative works.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings or beliefs are sincere and deeply held.

clue.text: German king just about controlled Italian port

indicators.note: about says the king's name goes around the next piece

parts.note: Otto was the name of several German kings and emperors
ran, as a business is run, means controlled

explanation.surface: A German king nearly controlled an Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' looks like 'nearly', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is a port town on the heel of Italy, in Apulia.

clue.text: Record son's snatched off fire

indicators.note: snatched off means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A record belonging to a son is snatched off the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is a fireplace or hearth fire, as in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a domestic fire or hearth.

clue.text: Ageing nurse, once given Eastern perfume

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a grade no longer used in Britain
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: An elderly nurse from the old days is given an oriental perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent describes something growing old or deteriorating with age.

clue.text: Result that disappoints regularly on field

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A team's dull result keeps happening on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'on field' give N, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A score of zero is a nothing result, a disappointing outcome in sport.

clue.text: Not bound to be lavish

definitions.meaning: not tied up or restricted, at liberty
generous, as when someone is ... with money

explanation.definitionFit: Free means at liberty and also open-handed, as in free with praise.

clue.text: Notoriously rejected work inside in overbearing way

indicators.note: inside means the reversed piece goes into the adverb

parts.note: arrant means notorious or utter, so arrantly means notoriously

indicators.note: rejected says the word is sent back, reading backwards

parts.note: go means work, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A notorious rejection of work done indoors, carried out arrogantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notoriously' looks like a scene-setting adverb, but it is the synonym that holds the turned-round work; arrant is an old word for notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting arrogantly means behaving in a haughty overbearing manner.

clue.text: Word books in French not allowed in Berlin

parts.note: a verb is a kind of word
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A word in French books is banned in Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Verboten is German for forbidden, hence 'in Berlin'.

clue.text: Some tigers at zoo not genuine

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the zoo's tigers are fakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute or imitation, not the real thing.

clue.text: Play Joplin number in new city dome

indicators.note: in means the rag sits inside the rearranged letters
new says the letters of the following words are made over

parts.note: Scott Joplin wrote ragtime pieces, or rags

explanation.surface: A Joplin piece is played in a new domed building in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CITY DOME into TICOMEDY, and RAG goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragicomedy is a play mixing tragic and comic elements.

clue.text: Discharge soldiers after action? It's a racket

indicators.note: after means the discharge and soldiers follow the action

parts.note: action in military language is a battle
to do a duty is to discharge it
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers are discharged after military action, which is described as a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a dismissal from service, but it means DO. A battledore is the bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is a small racket used to hit a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Oral test some'll put together for anniversary

indicators.note: oral says the following is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: test is try, and some'll is any'll

explanation.surface: Students' oral test answers are put together for an anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY plus ANY'LL, spoken together, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A triennial is an event or anniversary falling every third year.

clue.text: One spells out world fair riots with difficulty

parts.note: an expo is a large international exhibition

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are struggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A commentator explains rioting at a world fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An expositor is someone who explains or interprets, setting things out clearly.

clue.text: Compelled to retreat? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: to retreat means to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: made someone do it means compelled them

explanation.surface: Being forced to retreat is met with an unsympathetic 'Hard cheese!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is a British expression meaning bad luck; here it defines the Dutch semi-hard cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a firm Dutch cheese in a red wax rind.

clue.text: Judge famous poem about islands, hundreds of them

indicators.note: about turns the judge and poem round to read backwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A judge assesses a famous poem about islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns J and IF into FIJ; 'hundreds of them' refers to the islands, as Fiji is made of over three hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is a Pacific nation of several hundred islands, so it is hundreds of islands.

clue.text: Way to stop lie, etc, wrongly conveyed by ESP

indicators.note: to stop means plug a gap, so the path goes inside
wrongly says the letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: a path is a way

explanation.surface: Finding a way to stop lies being conveyed through ESP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges LIE ETC into TELEIC, and 'to stop' puts PATH in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathic communication is mind-to-mind transmission, the kind of extrasensory perception meant.

clue.text: Satire of so-called Ancient Mariner to receive booster

indicators.note: to receive means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Coleridge's wedding guest calls the Ancient Mariner a grey-beard loon
an amp, or amplifier, boosts a signal

explanation.surface: A satirical work about Coleridge's mariner receives a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of satirical writing ridiculing a person.

clue.text: Complain, whether there's good in it or not

definitions.text: Complain, whether there's good in it or not

indicators.note: in it means the letter sits inside the word

parts.note: to whine is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone complains whether or not things are going well.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says both words mean 'complain': with G in it or without, it still means grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is a British word for grumbling or complaining peevishly.

clue.text: Supplement old masters originally added to English course

indicators.note: added to means these pieces follow the English

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a supplement to a letter

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: A supplement on old masters is added to an English course.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse where the Derby is run.

clue.text: Quiet friend of Pooh dipping into mother's foodstuff

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside the next word

parts.note: mum is mother
sh is a request for quiet
Roo is a young kangaroo in the Winnie-the-Pooh stories

explanation.surface: A quiet friend of Winnie-the-Pooh dips into his mother's food.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are edible fungi, a common foodstuff.

clue.text: Eat greedily, being Edgar Allan's bird

definitions.meaning: to devour hungrily, to wolf food down
the black bird of Edgar Allan Poe's famous poem

explanation.surface: A Poe character's bird eats greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven is to devour; Poe's poem features a black bird of that name.

clue.text: Booty left on board in wet blanket

parts.note: spoils are booty
on board ship the left side is port

explanation.surface: Plunder left on a ship's deck turns up inside a wet blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins others' fun, which is what a wet blanket does.

clue.text: Movement in Swan Lake is almost finished

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: past means over and done with, finished

explanation.surface: A ballet sequence in Swan Lake is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: A pas is a ballet step, as in pas de deux; Swan Lake is a ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step or dance movement in ballet.

clue.text: Scene that's conveyed by Vaughan Williams, initially

indicators.note: conveyed by means carried inside the following letters
initially means the first letters of these names

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A scene is conveyed by the composer Vaughan Williams's music.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a scene or prospect seen from a place.

clue.text: One associated with daily events in the nursery?

definitions.text: One associated with daily events in the nursery?

parts.words: One associated with daily events in the nursery?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme character born on Monday, christened Tuesday and so on through the week to burial on Sunday

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme gives this character one life event for each day of the week.
